conventions: The English *with* standing before the complement of συναναμίγνυμι is given to the Greek dative, not to the supplied *keep company* frame: πόρνοις at 5:9 and τοιούτῳ at 5:11 take it under rule 21, as the articular datives τοῖς at 5:10 take it on the article. Rule 21's support-verb-frame clause, which would keep the preposition inside the verb's unit because the supplied noun *company* licenses it, is refused chapter-wide so that the four parallel datives read alike (rule 24); the 5:9 unit's note names that competing reading.

A supplied English completion on the indefinite τις is decided by what licenses it and not by the lemma. The generic noun of *any man* at 5:11 folds onto τις under rules 17 and 69, no other token being able to carry it; the partitive *of you* at 5:1 is `added` under rule 103, its content belonging to ἐν ὑμῖν, which the same verse has already spent on *among you*. Folding *of you* onto τινα as a rule 7 helper remains defensible and stands in that unit's note.
report: Read all 26 candidate lemma groups and the full dump end to end. No construction is analysed two ways without a source or ASV licence, so there are no patches.

ὁ is the only group with real internal variation. The T→ADV bucket puts 5:3 τὸν (…κατεργασάμενον) beside 5:12/5:13 τοὺς ἔξω/ἔσω, but the first governs a participle (rule 32, pronoun only, *him*) and the others a bare adverb (rule 31's verbless-modifier carve-out, *them that* on the article and the copula on the adverb). The T→N split between *the* and unrepresented tracks rules 19, 20, 23 and 38 exactly: every empty article either has its determiner slot occupied (5:2 τοῦτο, 5:4 and 5:7 ἡμῶν, 5:6 ὑμῶν, 5:10 τούτου) or is given no English determiner at all (5:3 twice, 5:5 τῷ Σατανᾷ, 5:13 ὁ θεός). 5:9 τῇ → *my* against 5:6 τὸ → unrepresented is rule 20's two arms, and the source licenses it: 5:6 has a genitive pronoun to take the possessive, 5:9 has none.

Substantival adjectives: 5:8 ἀζύμοις → *the unleavened bread* heads on the adjective, 5:13 τὸν πονηρόν gives *the … man* to the article and a bare *wicked* to the adjective. Opposite heads, but that is the article test rules 17, 58 and 102 require — the first phrase is anarthrous, the second articular.

ἐκ/ἐξ: 5:2 splits *from* / *among* because μέσου is expressed; 5:13 keeps *from among* whole on ἐξ because nothing else stands for it. 5:10 (*go* / *out of*) and 5:13 (*Put away* / *from among*) are rule 106's two arms, decided by the count of English words the ASV wrote — 5:10 writes one particle for preverb and preposition together, 5:13 writes *away* in addition to a complete *from among*.

Added-unit audit, which the lemma table cannot see: the chapter's two `added` units are 5:1 *of you* and 5:10 *meaning*, and every other supplied word is folded onto a token whose English it completes. The one near-split is the indefinite τις — *any man* folded at 5:11, *of you* added at 5:1 — and the two supplied words are of different kinds (a generic noun that only τις can license, against a partitive whose content ἐν ὑμῖν has already spent in the same verse). Recorded as a convention rather than patched; the 5:1 unit already names the competing fold.

The chapter is uniform on the English *with* before a dative complement: 5:9 πόρνοις, 5:10 τοῖς (twice, on the article) and εἰδωλολάτραις, 5:11 τοιούτῳ. Rule 21's support-verb-frame reading, which would have pulled *with* into the *keep company* unit at 5:9, is refused throughout. Recorded as a convention.

BSB: all four disagreements are articles the contract requires the ASV alignment to leave empty — 5:2 τὸ displaced by τοῦτο (rule 38), 5:4 τοῦ twice displaced by *our* (rule 20), 5:11 τῷ before a substantival demonstrative with no antecedent pronoun written (rule 49). None is an error. The 5:11 row is useful corroboration rather than a correction: BSB reads the *with* as realizing the dative case, which is exactly why this chapter puts it on τοιούτῳ under rule 49 instead of inside the verb frame.

No promotion. The one place the contract was stretched is 5:1 τοῦ πατρός → *his*, where rule 57's inner-article clause reaches a genitive under an anarthrous head noun; the clause decides the inner article 'separately and on its own phrase' and does not depend on an outer article, and one unit with no corpus support is not a basis for amending it.
